title: Local finite-field normal form for norm-algebraic-closure cocycles
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the extended norm topology, a finite intermediate extension $E$, a profinite group $G$, and a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action [def-pod-l-adic-representations]. Give $V_F=F\otimes_E W$ its finite-dimensional product topology for each intermediate $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, including $F=\Omega$; $G$ acts through $W$ and trivially on $F$. For a topological group $J$ and a topological $E$-vector space $V$ with continuous linear $J$-action define the ordinary nonnegative complex $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$ of abstract $E$-vector spaces, with $C^0_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=V$ and differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
For $n=0$ this reads $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. Cohomology means kernel modulo image in abstract $E$-vector spaces, with no closure of the coboundaries. For every integer $n\geq1$ and every $z\in C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega)$ with $dz=0$, there exist an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$, a finite intermediate extension $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, a continuous cocycle $u\in C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V_F)$, and a continuous cochain $b\in C^{n-1}_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V_\Omega)$ such that
$$z|_{H^n}=u+db$$
after the specified inclusion $V_F\hookrightarrow V_\Omega$. Here open means open in the profinite topology; no finite generation, finite cohomological dimension, completeness of $\Omega$, or discrete topology on $W$ is assumed. This is solely a statement about explicit continuous functions, with no identification with condensed derived invariants.

proof.text: Choose an $E$-basis of $W$, of size $d$. Thus $V_\Omega=\Omega^d$ and $V_F=F^d$ with the specified product topologies, and the action matrices have entries in $E$. Define the homogeneous cochain $f(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=g_0 z(g_0^{-1}g_1,g_1^{-1}g_2,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$. It is continuous and diagonally equivariant. In the alternating deletion differential, the term deleting $g_0$ is $g_1z(g_1^{-1}g_2,\ldots)$; factoring out $g_0$ makes it the first action term of $dz$. Deleting an interior $g_i$ multiplies the two adjacent ratios, while deleting $g_{n+1}$ gives the last term. Consequently $\delta f=g_0(dz)(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_n^{-1}g_{n+1})=0$. This calculation applies in every degree, including the degree-zero identity $\delta(g\mapsto gv)(g_0,g_1)=g_0((g_0^{-1}g_1)v-v)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent argument: explicit homogeneous coordinates.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover] to get an increasing sequence $F_j\supseteq E$. Each $V_{F_j}=F_j^d$ is closed in $\Omega^d$, since it is the intersection of the inverse images of the closed set $F_j$ under the finitely many coordinate projections. These subspaces cover $\Omega^d$: for each coordinate choose one $F_j$, then take the largest of the finitely many indices; if $d=0$, any index works. Put $A_j=f^{-1}(V_{F_j})$. These closed sets cover the nonempty compact Hausdorff space $G^{n+1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior] with $Y=X=G^{n+1}$; thus some $A_j$ has nonempty interior; write $F=F_j$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent argument: Baire applied to the compact source, not to the incomplete target.

proof.text: Choose a point $(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$ of that interior and a product of open neighbourhoods $U_0\times\cdots\times U_n$ contained in it. By the open-subgroup neighbourhood basis defining a profinite group, choose an open subgroup $H$ contained in $\bigcap_i U_i a_i^{-1}$. Then $H a_i\subseteq U_i$ for every $i$, so $f(Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n)\subseteq V_F$. Here left cosets $Ha_i$, rather than $a_iH$, are used, to make each coordinate an $H$-equivariant torsor for left multiplication.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent argument: product neighbourhood and profinite subgroup basis.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-finite-subfield-continuous-linear-retraction] to choose a continuous $E$-linear retraction $p_F:\Omega\to F$. Coordinatewise it gives $p:\Omega^d\to F^d$. Because every action matrix has entries in $E$, $p(gv)=g p(v)$ for all $g\in G$; this follows by applying $E$-linearity to each finite matrix sum. Regard $p$ also as an endomorphism of $V_\Omega$ and put $q=1-p$. Then $r=qf$ is a continuous homogeneous equivariant cocycle, since $q$ commutes with the action and the finite sums in $\delta$. It vanishes on $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$, since $q$ vanishes on $V_F$. Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-cocycle-rectangle-detection] with $K=E$, $M=V_\Omega$ and this open $H$ to obtain a continuous $H$-equivariant $t:H^n\to V_\Omega$ with $r|_{H^{n+1}}=\delta t$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent argument: retract the finite part and detect the remaining homogeneous class.

proof.text: Define $u=(pz)|_{H^n}$ and $b(h_1,\ldots,h_{n-1})=t(1,h_1,h_1h_2,\ldots,h_1\cdots h_{n-1})$. For $n=1$ this is the single vector $b=t(1)$. The function $u$ is continuous as an $F^d$-valued function, and $du=p(dz)|_{H^{n+1}}=0$. Evaluating $r=\delta t$ at $(1,h_1,h_1h_2,\ldots,h_1\cdots h_n)$ and using $H$-equivariance in its first deletion term gives $(z-u)(h_1,\ldots,h_n)=(db)(h_1,\ldots,h_n)$, by the same explicit deletion-to-ratio calculation of step 1. All these are finite evaluations and sums of continuous functions. Thus $z|_{H^n}=u+db$ with exactly the required coefficient inclusion. Rank zero, the trivial group, non-normal $H$, and degree one are included.

Reduced local finite-field normal form to Baire on the compact source and a generic rectangular homogeneous-cocycle detection lemma, after applying the existing continuous E-linear finite-field retraction. Added countable closed finite-field cover, generic rectangular detection, and a Baire Mathlib leaf.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-b1cca653d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the three new nodes and every cited statement (the retraction node included), the unit's direct-images proof paragraph (3), which does not contain this input (so proof_origin=agent is correct), L19 p.3 Prop 1.1.9 (countably many finite extensions plus Baire), and Mathlib Baire/Lemmas.lean:257 and LocallyCompactRegular.lean:23. I checked the five steps by hand. Step 1: the homogenization deletion terms match dz. Step 2: the F_j^d are closed, they cover because the sequence is increasing, and G^{n+1} is compact Hausdorff, so Baire applies. Step 3: U_i a_i^{-1} is a neighbourhood of 1, so the open subgroup H gives H a_i ⊆ U_i. Step 4: p commutes with the E-matrices, so (1-p)f is an equivariant cocycle that vanishes on the rectangle; the rectangle node applies with K=E, M=Ω^d. Step 5: dehomogenizing δt gives exactly the item's d, and n=1 gives b=t(1). The rectangle-detection node is true: n=1 checked explicitly, and in general by the colored-join argument (the join is acyclic through degree n-1, its degree-n simplices are exactly the rectangle, and the homotopy runs through degree n). It is generic and is not a clause of the item. The countable-cover node is true (finitely many extensions of each degree, composita with E, closed because finite-dimensional over complete Q_ℓ). The Baire leaf is an exact Mathlib match. I found no duplicates in an rg -L search of the DAG, no SGA, no route departure, no cycle, and the only citer (profinite-algcl-derived-invariants-comparison step 7) uses the item as stated.
